Shamballa Ho Chi Minh is a classic case of style over substance.
Jan 2026 • Family
Yes, the setting and ambience are undeniably beautiful. The space is serene, thoughtfully designed, and gives the impression of a refined dining experience. Unfortunately, that’s where the positives end.

Service levels are frankly lacklustre. Staff taking orders have a very poor command of English and were unable to recommend a single dish when asked. When I enquired about popular or signature items, the only response was to push a set menu—completely missing the point of the question. It felt lazy rather than helpful.

The food itself is wildly inconsistent. The tofu and cassava salad were decent, though hardly memorable. The momos were just passable—certainly not something you’d expect at these prices.

The worst offender was the outrageously priced truffle green curry. There was not even the faintest hint of truffle flavour. After complaining, they added “more truffle”, yet it still tasted nothing like truffle. I seriously doubt real truffle was used at all.

To make matters worse, this place is terrible at accommodating children. There are no child-friendly options on the menu, and when I asked if they could prepare something as simple as a basic noodle soup, the staff appeared completely panicked and unable to handle the request. For a restaurant positioning itself at this price point, that’s simply unacceptable.

In summary, this place charges international prices but delivers third-rate food and service. As an international and business traveller who has dined extensively around the world, I can confidently say this restaurant offers poor value, poor quality, and poor service.

Avoid.

Heavily overpriced for what it had to offer

Let me start with the positive things: Shamballa has a nice ambiance and offers a quiet space in the very loud and hectic city of Saigon. The staff is trying hard to make you feel welcome and there is no crazy karaoke music in the back. It also didn’t take long for us to get some food which was presented beautifully (good looking salad and cute clay pots for the entrees). It offers a huge amount of dishes and drinks (which in case of food I don’t necessarily think is a good thing as I prefer a restaurant which has only a couple of options, which are all very authentic and taste good but that of course is only my opinion).
Our meal started out good with a salad that looked very nice and tasted good. It was very refreshing. Whether it was worth the price is up for debate but so far so good. Unfortunately it went downhill from there. Our other two dishes were a banana curry which was tasting alright (not bad but nothing special) and something with buckwheat vegetables and a sauce. While the sauce tasted good and all the produce had good quality, the vegetables tasted boring and there was way to much buckwheat and too little sauce. Also the buckwheat had a distinct taste of socks.
The prices where extremely high for Vietnamese standards and didn’t include VAT or service charge. While the fine print actually pointed this out it was the first time in Vietnam prices where stated excluding such fees and since I wanted to have dinner and not read a legal paper I overlooked it. Overall it was the priciest meal of our 30 day journey but it was also among the most unsatisfying ones, even without considering the cost. My girlfriend and I had great meals for 15-20% of what we spent at Shamballas.
If your dinner expectations are more about service drinks and ambience you might consider coming here. I personally am more interested in the food itself, which is why I would definitely not come again. One can pay with credit card which is a good thing though. It was a pity to see a restaurant that does almost everything right except for the food…
